brief.what: Article 11 rewrites parts of the zoning bylaw to match recent changes to the state Zoning Act: variances would turn on "practical difficulty" instead of "substantial hardship", some additions to older nonconforming homes would be allowed without a special permit, a nonconforming use would be lost after four years of abandonment instead of two, and a permit's protection would run twenty-four months instead of six.
brief.next: Two-thirds vote required (the warrant says so), then Attorney General review.

stories.dek: The Planning Board meets Wednesday, Oct 28. The agenda lists an item on zoning changes.

brief.what: A standing placeholder for zoning bylaw amendments the Planning Board is working on: residential facilities for residents 55 years of age or older (the Clemmey proposal), two B4 Zoning District changes (the commercial component and multifamily housing by special permit), a permitting clarification for the North Main Street Overlay District, and new or amended uses under Section 230-3.5 such as coworking offices, pet services, food incubators and makerspaces. Also on the list: Parkway/Transit Oriented Development, scenic road and inclusionary zoning ideas from individual members, and the board's own rules and fees.
brief.history: Also on the Sep 23 Planning Board agenda.

brief.what: Same item, flagged twice. Woodland Ridge, LLC (through attorney Melissa Robbins of Farrell, & Robbins, P.C.) wants a 40B comprehensive permit for 40 single-family homes for sale on 45.5 acres between Bancroft Street and Orion Road: 32 two-bedroom and 8 three-bedroom homes, with 10 of them (25%) affordable to households at or below 80% of area median income.
